data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 defends §11.3 flags as a bookkeeping false positive but commits a causal-break fallacy: it asserts that nu verdicts (SRC_006, SRC_008) validating per-critic adjudication 'do not validate that the aggregate ritual-level flag is correctly derived from those verdicts,' then leaps to the conclusion that the flag is therefore spurious. The invalidity of one validation pathway does not entail the invalidity of the derived flag — the aggregation layer could be independently sound. SRC_001 offers zero evidence of an actual stale-state or double-counting bug; it merely names the bug class and asserts it exists. Under §11.3, a sustained flag requires a genuine failure event; SRC_001's own logic concedes the underlying failure (a critic failing on SRC_005) is real and correctly adjudicated, so recording it at the aggregate level is not a spurious duplication but a legitimate roll-up. The target thus fails the audit standard because it cannot show the flag is a false positive — it can only show that one layer of validation does not cover another, which is an argument from ignorance, not a refutation.
